==English==

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|craven}}, from {{inh|en|ang|crafian|t=to crave, ask, implore, demand, summon}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*krafōn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*krafjaną|t=to demand}}. Cognate with {{cog|da|kræve|t=to demand, require}}, {{cog|sv|kräva|t=to crave, demand}}, {{cog|is|krefja|t=to demand}}, {{cog|no|kreve|t=to demand}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|krāv}}, {{IPA|en|/kɹeɪv/}}
* {{rhymes|en|eɪv|s=1}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-crave.ogg|a=US}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To [[desire]] strongly, so as to satisfy an [[appetite]]; to [[long]] or [[yearn]] for.
#: {{ux|en|to '''crave''' for peace}}{{ux|en|to '''crave''' after wealth}}{{ux|en|to '''crave''' drugs}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|archaic|or|literary}} To [[ask]] for earnestly; to [[beg]] or [[demand]], as from a figure of [[authority]].
#: {{ux|en|I humbly '''crave''' your indulgence to read this letter until the end.}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|Mark|15|43||Joseph {{...}} went in boldly unto Pilate, and '''craved''' the body of Jesus.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[call for]]; to require as a course of action.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Julius Caesar|2|1|text=It is the bright day that brings forth the adder and that '''craves''' wary walking}}
